units.hebrew: בָּרוּךְ שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם. בָּרוּךְ הוּא. בָּרוּךְ עוֹשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית. בָּרוּךְ אוֹמֵר וְעוֹשֶׂה. בָּרוּךְ גּוֹזֵר וּמְקַיֵּם. בָּרוּךְ מְרַחֵם עַל הָאָרֶץ. בָּרוּךְ מְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת. בָּרוּךְ מְשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר טוֹב לִירֵאָיו. בָּרוּךְ חַי לָעַד וְקַיָּם לָנֶצַח. בָּרוּךְ פּוֹדֶה וּמַצִּיל. בָּרוּךְ שְׁמוֹ.
units.transliteration: Baruch she’amar ve’hayah ha’olam. Baruch hu. Baruch oseh bereishit. Baruch omer ve’oseh. Baruch gozer umekayem. Baruch merachem al ha’aretz. Baruch merachem al habriyot. Baruch meshalem sachar tov liy’re’av. Baruch chai la’ad vekayam lanetzach. Baruch podeh umatzil. Baruch shemo.
units.english: Blessed is He who spoke, and the world came into being. Blessed is He. Blessed is He who makes the beginning. Blessed is He who speaks and does. Blessed is He who decrees and fulfills. Blessed is He who has mercy on the earth. Blessed is He who has mercy on the creatures. Blessed is He who pays a good reward to those who fear Him. Blessed is He who lives forever and endures to eternity. Blessed is He who redeems and rescues. Blessed is His name.
units.commentary: This opening of Pesukei Dezimra affirms God as the Creator who brings the world into being through speech. The kavannah is acknowledging divine creative power at the start of the morning praises and connecting the words to our own speech and actions throughout the day.
units.kavannahPrompt: As you begin Pesukei Dezimra, pause on the words 'who spoke and the world came into being.' What does it mean for you today that creation continues through divine speech?

units.hebrew: אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ, עוֹד יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה.
units.transliteration: Ashrei yoshvei veitecha, od yehalelucha selah.
units.english: Happy are those who dwell in Your house; they will yet praise You, selah.
units.commentary: Ashrei opens with a verse from Psalm 84 before Psalm 145. The image is of dwelling in God's house: prayer as a place we return to and stay in, not only visit.
units.kavannahPrompt: Where do you feel 'at home' in your davening? Bring that sense of dwelling to Ashrei today.

units.hebrew: יִשְׁתַּבַּח שִׁמְךָ לָעַד מַלְכֵּנוּ, הָאֵל הַמֶּלֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ.
units.transliteration: Yishtabach shimcha la’ad malkeinu, ha’El hamelech hagadol vehakadosh bashamayim uva’aretz.
units.english: May Your name be praised forever, our King, the God, the great and holy King, in heaven and on earth.
units.commentary: Yishtabach closes Pesukei Dezimra, sealing the section that Baruch She'amar opened. The two blessings frame the psalms between them.
units.kavannahPrompt: As you reach Yishtabach, notice the transition: the praises are complete and you are preparing for Barchu and the Shema.
